rationale: C08 provides the strongest concrete template for the child's recitals: both identify an earlier executive order granting a retirement exemption for an indefinite period bounded by the officer's appointment or term, then invoke the President's judgment about what the public interest requires. The child materially adapts that established exemption-extension structure to revoke a group exemption because the public interest no longer requires it. C14 is highly similar but slightly less close in its wording; C15 shares the same machinery in a more compressed form.

shared_material.child_excerpt: certain officers and employees ... were exempted from automatic separation ... for an indefinite period of time not extending beyond the duration of their appointment or term of service
shared_material.parent_excerpt: was by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] ... exempted from compulsory retirement for age for an indefinite period of time not extending beyond the duration of his appointment or term of office
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel description of a prior retirement exemption, including the same indefinite-period limitation tied to appointment or term.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest no longer requires the exemption
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that the said Clyde B. Aitchison be further exempted
shared_material.explanation: The child reverses the same presidential public-interest finding used to justify continuation of the exemption.
The matching recital-to-operative transition reinforces the shared drafting structure, though it is not independently probative.
